title: Chapter 5 Mastery Quiz: Survey Design & Correlational Research
description: Demonstrate mastery of question writing, probability sampling, Pearson's r, and the perils of spurious correlations.

questions.question: Which of the following is the defining flaw of a 'double-barreled' survey item?

options.text: It asks participants about two separate issues within a single sentence, permitting only one response
It uses two different languages simultaneously
It requires the respondent to answer the question twice
It contains a typo in the second word

questions.explanation: Double-barreled questions combine two distinct attitudes or issues, making it impossible to determine which issue the participant's response addresses.

questions.question: A survey item reads: 'Do you agree with leading health experts that sugar-sweetened beverages should be heavily taxed?' What type of flawed item is this?

options.text: A leading question
A double-negative question
An unobtrusive trace measure
A ratio measurement scale

questions.explanation: Leading questions subtly prompt or encourage the respondent toward a particular answer by citing authoritative consensus or using biased wording.

questions.question: What is Social Desirability Bias?

options.text: The preference for participating in group experiments rather than solo studies
The tendency of respondents to answer questions in a manner that will be viewed favorably by others
The tendency for attractive researchers to obtain higher survey response rates
A cognitive bias in which people desire more social media followers

questions.explanation: Social desirability bias leads participants to over-report positive, virtuous behaviors and under-report embarrassing, unhealthy, or taboo actions.

questions.question: How do researchers systematically detect and counteract 'acquiescence bias' (the tendency to agree with all statements)?

options.text: By incorporating reverse-worded (reverse-scored) items throughout the survey
By making all questions open-ended essays
By increasing the font size of the survey instructions
By administering the survey only at midnight

questions.explanation: Reverse-scored items require disagreeing to express a positive trait, allowing researchers to flag respondents who unthinkingly agree with every item.

questions.question: What is the defining condition of Simple Random Sampling?

options.text: Participants are selected by posting flyers in public university cafeterias
Every individual in the defined target population has an equal, non-zero probability of being chosen
The researcher picks whoever looks friendliest on the street
Participants choose whether they want to be in the study or not

questions.explanation: In simple random sampling, every single member of the target population has an exact, equal mathematical probability of selection.

questions.question: A polling firm divides a state population into racial and ethnic subgroups, then randomly samples individuals from each subgroup in exact proportion to the state census. What sampling method is this?

options.text: Stratified random sampling
Snowball sampling
Convenience sampling
Naturalistic observation

questions.explanation: Stratified random sampling divides the population into meaningful demographic strata and draws random samples from each stratum proportionally.

questions.question: Why is convenience sampling (such as using an undergraduate psychology subject pool) vulnerable to external validity criticism?

options.text: College students are all identical clones
The sample may not be representative of the broader, diverse human population (the WEIRD problem)
College students are prohibited from answering survey questions by federal law
It produces perfect negative correlations in every study

questions.explanation: Convenience samples often over-represent educated, young, affluent, western demographics, limiting generalizability to wider populations.

questions.question: A researcher sends a postal survey to 1,000 citizens, but only 80 people return it (an 8% response rate). What critical methodological threat does this introduce?

options.text: Non-response bias (those who replied may differ systematically from those who did not)
Type I Alpha error
The Hawthorne effect
Violation of Occam's Razor

questions.explanation: A low response rate creates non-response bias because individuals who choose to complete a survey often have stronger opinions or more free time than the majority.

questions.question: What is the theoretical range of Pearson's correlation coefficient (r)?

options.text: From negative infinity to positive infinity

questions.explanation: Pearson's r is mathematically constrained between -1.00 (perfect negative linear relationship) and +1.00 (perfect positive linear relationship).

questions.question: A psychologist finds that as hours of weekly aerobic exercise increase, scores on a clinical depression inventory consistently decrease. What type of correlation is this?

options.text: Positive correlation
Negative (inverse) correlation
Curvilinear zero correlation
Spurious correlation

questions.explanation: When increases in one variable correspond systematically to decreases in another variable, the correlation is negative (inverse).

questions.question: Which of the following correlation coefficients represents the WEAKEST linear relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation: Correlation strength is measured by its absolute value distance from zero (|r|). |-0.07| = 0.07, which is closest to zero and thus the weakest.

questions.question: What graphical chart is universally used to visualize the bivariate relationship between two continuous quantitative variables?

options.text: Pie chart
Scatterplot
Stacked bar graph
Flowchart diagram

questions.explanation: A scatterplot displays individual data points across X and Y axes, allowing immediate visual inspection of linear and non-linear bivariate patterns.

questions.question: If a scatterplot reveals points arranged in a wide, circular cloud with no discernible upward or downward slant, what is the approximate correlation coefficient?
questions.explanation: A diffuse circular cloud with flat regression slope indicates that changes in X do not predict changes in Y (zero correlation).

questions.question: What is the primary danger of calculating Pearson's r on data that have a 'curvilinear' relationship (like test anxiety and exam scores)?

options.text: The computer will crash
Pearson's r only detects straight linear lines, so it will falsely report a near-zero correlation despite a strong relationship
Pearson's r will report a value greater than +1.00
It violates the Belmont Report

questions.explanation: Pearson's r evaluates exclusively linear trends; an inverted U-curve has opposing slopes that cancel out mathematically to near r = 0.

questions.question: What effect does 'restriction of range' have on a correlation coefficient?

options.text: It artificially reduces (deflates) the apparent strength of the correlation
It artificially inflates the correlation to near +1.00
It reverses the sign of the correlation from positive to negative
It has zero impact on correlation magnitude

questions.explanation: When the variance of one or both variables is truncated or restricted, the calculated correlation coefficient is artificially diminished.

questions.question: In a cross-sectional study, researchers find that adolescents who play more hours of violent video games commit more acts of school vandalism. What is the 'directionality problem'?

options.text: We cannot determine whether playing violent games causes vandalism, or whether vandalistic tendencies lead teens to choose violent games
The games were manufactured in another country
Vandalism is an illegal act that cannot be studied
The survey had fewer than 10 questions

questions.explanation: Because both variables were measured concurrently, it is impossible to determine which variable occurred first temporally to cause the other.

questions.question: What is the 'third-variable problem' in correlational research?

options.text: Having to pay three different researchers to enter data
An unmeasured external variable may be the true common cause of both correlated variables, creating a spurious link
A study that lasts more than three years
Using three questionnaires in the same battery

questions.explanation: The third-variable problem occurs when an unmeasured confounding factor (Z) drives the observed statistical association between X and Y.

questions.question: A classic study found that the number of churches in a city correlates strongly and positively with the number of crime arrests in that city. What third variable explains this spurious relationship?

options.text: Total city population size
Average church choir volume
The price of communion wafers
Police vehicle horsepower

questions.explanation: Larger cities naturally have both more churches and more total crimes simply because they contain many more people.

questions.question: What statistical technique allows researchers to evaluate the correlation between Variable X and Variable Y while mathematically holding a third confounding variable (Z) constant?

options.text: Partial Correlation
Independent samples t-test
Chi-Square test of independence
Inter-rater reliability analysis

questions.explanation: Partial correlation quantifies the linear relationship between two variables while statistically controlling and removing the influence of one or more covariates.

questions.question: How does a longitudinal 'cross-lagged panel design' help address the directionality problem?

options.text: By measuring both variables at multiple points in time, allowing researchers to evaluate which variable temporally precedes changes in the other
By randomly assigning participants to take surveys in different rooms
By eliminating the need for informed consent
By automatically making all survey responses anonymous

questions.explanation: Cross-lagged designs track whether Variable A at Time 1 predicts Variable B at Time 2 more robustly than Variable B at Time 1 predicts Variable A at Time 2.

questions.question: What is the coefficient of determination (r^2) in correlational statistics?

options.text: The square root of the sample size
The proportion of variance in one variable that is predictable from or shared with the other variable
The probability that the null hypothesis is true
The standard error of measurement

questions.explanation: Squaring the correlation coefficient (r^2) gives the proportion of shared or explained variance between the two variables.

questions.question: If the correlation between childhood exposure to music lessons and spatial cognitive ability is r = 0.50, what percentage of the variance in spatial ability is shared with music lessons?
questions.explanation: The percentage of shared variance is r^2 * 100: (0.50)^2 = 0.25, which corresponds to 25% of shared variance.
